entries.question: What is the Digital Health Analysis report?
entries.answer: It is an audit of how your dealership shows up on Google: your Google Business Profile, your Google Maps listing, and the structured data on your website. It lists what is working, what is missing, and what to fix.

entries.question: Can I check these findings myself?
entries.answer: Yes, most of them. Search your business on Google and open your Business Profile, look at your homepage for visible reviews, and view your website page source and search for application/ld+json to see your structured data.

entries.question: What is the Digital Health Alert?
entries.answer: It is the short three-screen version of the audit. It shows the most important alerts first and then leads you to the full report.

entries.question: How was the audit done?
entries.answer: It was done directly. We reviewed your Google Business Profile and Maps listing, read the structured data in your website code, and looked at your website pages in a browser. Counts such as reviews are as of the audit date shown on the report.

entries.question: What do Audit Verified and Inferred mean?
entries.answer: Audit Verified means the finding was directly confirmed during the audit. Inferred means it is a logical conclusion from verified facts and was not tested directly, for example how an AI engine might treat your business.

entries.question: Will the numbers on my report change?
entries.answer: Yes. Counts such as review totals and the date of your last post are as of the audit date on the report. They change over time, and the report is refreshed when it is re-sent.

entries.question: Does the report guarantee results?
entries.answer: No. The report does not guarantee rankings, calls, or sales. The result figures shown are results across 21 Mitsubishi dealer locations, not projections for your dealership.

entries.question: How is Reviews and Reputation scored?
entries.answer: It looks at your Google rating, how recently reviews arrive, whether you respond, how Facebook compares, and whether real reviews show on your website. Recent-review windows are 15 days for Sales, 30 for Service, and 90 for Parts.

entries.question: What makes a Profile Completeness score of 10?
entries.answer: All three listings exist, Sales, Service, and Parts, and every checklist item is complete on each. A combined Service and Parts listing counts for both departments.

entries.question: Why does my status say Critical if my average is above 5?
entries.answer: There is a weakest-link rule. If any single category scores 2 out of 10 or lower, the overall status is Critical no matter what the average is. One very weak area can hold the rest back.

entries.question: How were the category ratings decided?
entries.answer: Each category is scored from what the audit found, against a fixed rubric. They are not produced by an automated scoring tool. The overall score is the simple average of those eight ratings.

entries.question: What is Profile Completeness?
entries.answer: It rates how complete your Google listings are for Sales, Service, and Parts. Each listing that exists earns points, and earns more as its checklist is completed. All three listings, fully complete, score 10.

entries.question: How are the two schema categories scored?
entries.answer: One looks at structure: schema on your key pages, department entries, and their own page addresses and phones. The other looks at fields such as name, address, hours, logo, sameAs, areaServed, hasMap, and services. Both score presence only.

entries.question: How is Maps and NAP Consistency scored?
entries.answer: It checks that your name, address, and phone match between Google and your website, and across five directories, plus correct department phones and a correct map pin.

entries.question: How was my score calculated?
entries.answer: The report rates eight categories from zero to ten and averages them equally. The eight are: GBP claimed and verified, profile completeness, photos, reviews and reputation, GBP posts and engagement, Maps and NAP consistency, local business schema, and schema field completeness.

entries.question: What does the Profile Completeness checklist include?
entries.answer: Categories, hours for that department, phone number, website link, services or products listed, business description, and attributes. The Service listing also needs a scheduling link.

entries.question: What does the overall score mean?
entries.answer: It is a zero to ten summary of how well your Google presence is set up today. Higher is better. Under 5 is Critical, 5 to 6.9 is Major Issues, and 7 or higher is Needs Improvement or Strong.

entries.question: What if I only have a Sales listing?
entries.answer: A complete Sales listing can earn up to 4 of 10 points: 2 for having it and 2 for complete information. Service and Parts listings add the other 6.

entries.question: What does the slider on the first screen show?
entries.answer: It shows your overall score on a zero to ten scale. The marks are 0 Critical, 5 Major Issues, and 10 Fully Optimized.

entries.question: What does a very low score on GBP Posts mean?
entries.answer: It means the audit found little or no recent posting activity on the Google Business Profile. The report shows the date of the last post as of the audit date.

entries.question: What does a 10 mean in the report?
entries.answer: A 10 means every item in that category was fully met in the audit. Any category at 2 or lower sets the overall status to Critical.

entries.question: How are the Photos and Posts scores decided?
entries.answer: They are rated against a standard we set, not a Google requirement: one new photo a week per profile, and 8 posts a month for Sales and 4 each for Service and Parts. Photo posts count for both.

entries.question: What if Service and Parts are one combined listing?
entries.answer: A combined Service and Parts listing earns the points for both departments. The report also notes whether the main listing shows the department links.

entries.question: What is schema completeness?
entries.answer: It is how fully the structured data on your website describes your business, location, services, and links to your other profiles.

entries.question: What is AI search visibility?
entries.answer: It is how often AI answers, such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity, cite or recommend your business. This is an industry definition. The report rates it qualitatively and did not test every AI engine.

entries.question: What is sameAs?
entries.answer: sameAs is a schema.org property that lists web addresses of other official pages for the same business, such as social profiles. Google does not document a specific ranking effect, so the report treats any effect as inferred.

entries.question: What is a Google Business Profile?
entries.answer: It is your free business listing on Google Search and Google Maps. It shows your name, address, phone number, hours, photos, reviews, and posts.

entries.question: What is areaServed?
entries.answer: areaServed is a schema.org property that states the cities or regions a business serves. When it is missing, your structured data does not say which markets you serve.

entries.question: What is local authority?
entries.answer: It is how well-known and trusted your business is locally, measured by reviews, links, and citations. It is not an official Google term. Google's own term is prominence.

entries.question: What is omni-social distribution?
entries.answer: Every Google Business Profile post is also shared on Facebook, Instagram, Threads, LinkedIn, Pinterest, and Bluesky, rewritten for each platform. It is in addition to the profile posts, not instead of them.

entries.question: What is a Knowledge Panel?
entries.answer: It is the information box Google can show in search results about a business.

entries.question: What is NAP consistency?
entries.answer: NAP means name, address, and phone number. Consistency means they match everywhere your business is listed online, including Google and directories.

entries.question: What is structured data or schema?
entries.answer: It is code on your website, usually in a format called JSON-LD, that labels facts such as your business name, address, departments, and profile links so search engines can read them. Google says structured data helps it understand the content of a page.

entries.question: What is the Map Pack?
entries.answer: It is the group of local business listings with a map that Google shows for local searches, such as service near me.

entries.question: What is hasMap?
entries.answer: hasMap is a schema.org property that points to a map of the business, typically its Google Maps listing. An older property called map is used for the same purpose. Google does not document an effect on your Business Profile, so the report treats any effect as inferred.

entries.question: What do SEO, AEO, and GEO mean?
entries.answer: SEO is search engine optimization, for ranking in search results. AEO is answer engine optimization, for answer-style results. GEO is generative engine optimization, for AI-generated answers. The report's content strategy covers all three.

entries.question: What is the Departments line on a listing?
entries.answer: On a properly built main Sales listing, a Departments line shows a separate link for each department listing, such as Service and Parts. A combined listing shows as one link.

entries.question: What are department entities?
entries.answer: They are separate entries in your website code for Sales, Service, and Parts. Having them in your website code is a separate fact from having Sales, Service, and Parts listings on Google. The report checks both.

entries.question: What is GBP structure?
entries.answer: It is how completely your Google Business Profile is built: categories, department profiles, services, attributes, and hours.

entries.question: Why does the report mention how long ago my last post was?
entries.answer: The audit records the date of your last Google Business Profile post. Regular posts keep the profile current for customers, and posting activity is one of the eight rated categories.

entries.question: Why does the report say my reviews are not shown on my website?
entries.answer: The audit checks whether your Google reviews appear on your website for visitors. If they do not, visitors have to leave your site to see them. The report recommends showing them visibly on the page.

entries.question: Why does the report compare Google and Facebook reviews?
entries.answer: It compares your review counts and ratings across platforms as of the audit date. A large gap between platforms is something customers can see.

entries.question: Why do missing Service and Parts profiles matter?
entries.answer: Each department can have its own Google listing. If only Sales has one, Service and Parts searches have no matching department listing from you on Google. Your website code may already describe those departments. What is missing is the Google listing.

entries.question: Should my reviews be added to my website schema?
entries.answer: No. Google's guidelines say reviews a business writes about itself, including through a widget on its own site, are not eligible for star results, so the report does not recommend review markup. It recommends showing real reviews visibly on the page.

entries.question: When do content articles and photo posts begin publishing?
entries.answer: Articles, GEO-optimized posts, and photos begin publishing in the first weeks after onboarding and compound over time.

entries.question: How many online directories are included in listing syndication?
entries.answer: Listing information is syndicated and updated across more than 60 online directories.

entries.question: What work begins on day one?
entries.answer: Initial profile setup, name, address, and phone consistency, categories, and nesting the Service and Parts profiles begin immediately.

entries.question: How often are directory listings updated?
entries.answer: The listing information is kept accurate and syndicated 24/7 across online directories.

entries.question: How often are SEO content articles posted?
entries.answer: The program includes weekly SEO-optimized content articles.

entries.question: How often are custom visuals created for social posts?
entries.answer: Custom visuals are created weekly for omni-social posts.

entries.question: Is the local business schema build included in the CLIKsearch program?
entries.answer: Yes. The CLIKsearch program includes the Local Business Schema build and delivery. We provide a full schema analysis consult, and the schema is the fix.

entries.question: Who answers reviews on the profiles?
entries.answer: AI-powered review answering is included and operates 24/7.

entries.question: What does the KPI reporting track?
entries.answer: The reporting includes measures such as web visits, vehicle detail page views, map views, driving directions, calls, foot traffic, and reviews.

entries.question: Is omni-social distribution included in every plan?
entries.answer: Yes. Omni-social distribution is included in every plan at no additional cost.

entries.question: Are dealership photo posts optimized for local discovery?
entries.answer: The program includes GEO-optimized photo posts. The photos can use location-specific information.

entries.question: Which dealership listings can the Reputation Review Reactivation Builder Campaign target?
entries.answer: The campaign can target past customers for Sales, Service, and Parts listings through automated email and text-message workflows.

entries.question: Do I have to build the schema myself?
entries.answer: No. CLIKsearch builds and delivers the Local Business Schema as part of the program, along with a full schema analysis consult.

entries.question: Does the service include map-pack management?
entries.answer: Yes. Map-pack management and local SEO are included across the Sales, Service, and Parts profiles.

entries.question: Is the Google Business Profile service fully managed?
entries.answer: Yes. Sales, Service, and Parts profiles are fully managed and monitored 24/7.

entries.question: Are the Service and Parts profiles nested?
entries.answer: Yes. The 3-Pack includes a Sales profile, with Service and Parts profiles nested.

entries.question: What is the CLIKsearch solution when a dealership has low Google or Facebook reviews?
entries.answer: The solution is CLIKsearch's Reputation Review Reactivation Builder Campaign. It sends automated emails and text messages to past customers to help grow a steady stream of reviews on both Google Business Profile and Facebook.

entries.question: Does the service check name, address, and phone consistency?
entries.answer: Yes. Keeping name, address, and phone information consistent across listings is part of the optimization strategy.

entries.question: What can the custom local dealership website schema describe?
entries.answer: It can describe the dealership, its Sales, Service, and Parts departments, and its services, and include links from the website to its profiles.

entries.question: Do Facebook and Instagram posts include engagement comments?
entries.answer: Yes. Facebook and Instagram posts include automatic engagement comments.

entries.question: How many Google Business Profile posts and photos are included each month?
entries.answer: The monthly maximum is 8 for Sales, 4 for Service, and 4 for Parts, for up to 16 posts and photos total.

entries.question: Will I get 62 percent more local search traffic?
entries.answer: The 62 percent figure is the year-over-year increase in Google Maps mobile views across 21 Mitsubishi dealer locations. It is a past result, not a promise for your dealership.

entries.question: What results can I expect?
entries.answer: Results vary by dealership, and nothing is guaranteed. CLIKsearch's commitment is go-live in 72 hours after onboarding and results within 90 days. I can share what other Mitsubishi dealers have seen, or help you book a time to talk it through.

entries.question: What results have other Mitsubishi dealers seen?
entries.answer: Across 21 Mitsubishi dealer locations on CLIKsearch, 2024 compared with the prior year: website visits up 29 percent, mobile calls up 28.7 percent, driving directions up 47.8 percent, and Google Maps mobile views up 62.4 percent. These are past results, not a promise for your dealership.

entries.answer: CLIKsearch fixes and manages them for you. The commitment is go-live in 72 hours after onboarding and results within 90 days. It does not promise specific rankings or lead numbers. To get started, book a time now, or activate in the MiDS Portal.
